title: SOC Analyst Career Roadmap: From Fundamentals to Advanced Threat Detection & Response
description: A comprehensive roadmap for aspiring and current Security Operations Center (SOC) Analysts, covering essential IT foundations, networking, operating systems, log management, SIEM operations, alert triage, incident response, threat intelligence, detection engineering, threat hunting, and practical lab environments to build a robust SOC portfolio.

tree.name: Cybersecurity & IT Foundations
tree.description: Build a solid understanding of fundamental IT concepts including networking, operating systems, cloud basics, and core cybersecurity principles necessary for effective security analysis.

resources.title: Learn Linux in 5 Days (Free Code Camp)

children.name: Networking & Operating System Essentials for SOC
children.description: Master TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/S, common network devices, security implications of protocols, Windows internals (Event Logs, PowerShell for security), and Linux fundamentals (syslog, bash scripting for security tasks). This forms the bedrock for understanding security events and initial investigation.

children.name: Cloud Security Fundamentals
children.description: Understand core cloud computing models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS), the shared responsibility model, and foundational cloud security concepts relevant to monitoring and incident response in cloud environments (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP).

children.name: Core Cybersecurity Principles
children.description: Grasp the CIA Triad, risk management basics, vulnerability vs. exploit, common security controls (administrative, technical, physical), and authentication mechanisms like MFA, SSO, and IAM concepts.

tree.name: Threat Landscape & Intelligence
tree.description: Learn about common attack vectors, malware types, and how to utilize threat intelligence frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK to understand and categorize adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs).

resources.title: OWASP Top 10 Web Application Security Risks

children.name: Common Attack Vectors & Techniques
children.description: Identify and understand the mechanics of various attacks including phishing, malware (ransomware, trojans, worms), web application attacks (OWASP Top 10), network attacks (DDoS, sniffing), and common post-exploitation techniques.

resources.title: Phishing Attacks: How They Work and How to Stop Them

children.name: Introduction to Threat Intelligence
children.description: Explore the different types of threat intelligence (strategic, operational, tactical), understand Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) and Indicators of Attack (IOAs), and learn to apply the MITRE ATT&CK framework for threat analysis and mapping.

resources.title: Using MITRE ATT&CK in Your SOC

children.name: Cyber Kill Chain & Unified Kill Chain
children.description: Understand classic attack frameworks like the Lockheed Martin Cyber Kill Chain and the Unified Kill Chain to better comprehend the stages of an adversary's operation and how to disrupt them.

children.name: Malware Analysis Fundamentals
children.description: Gain a foundational understanding of various malware types, their infection vectors, and basic static and dynamic analysis techniques to aid in identifying and triaging malware-related alerts.

tree.name: Log Management & SIEM Operations
tree.description: Gain proficiency in collecting, aggregating, normalizing, searching, and analyzing security logs using Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) platforms to identify anomalous activities and potential threats.

children.name: Critical Log Sources & Telemetry
children.description: Identify and understand critical log sources from Windows (Event Logs, Sysmon), Linux (syslog, auditd), network devices (firewalls, routers, proxies), Active Directory, cloud environments (e.g., CloudTrail, Azure Activity Logs), and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) solutions.

children.name: Data Ingestion & Normalization
children.description: Learn how logs are collected using various agents (e.g., Winlogbeat, rsyslog, filebeat, data connectors) and the basics of parsing, normalization, data enrichment, and data modeling (e.g., CIM, ECS) for efficient analysis in a SIEM. Understand common log formats like CEF and LEEF.

children.name: SIEM Querying, Alerting & Reporting
children.description: Develop advanced search skills using SIEM query languages (e.g., SPL for Splunk, KQL for Sentinel, EQL for Elastic). Practice correlating events across diverse data sources, building effective detection rules, reducing false positives, creating dashboards, and generating reports.

children.name: Hands-on SIEM Practice & Scenarios
children.description: Apply SIEM knowledge through practical exercises and simulated scenarios. Practice investigating common security incidents using a SIEM, honing skills in data exploration, alert validation, and initial analysis within different SIEM platforms.

resources.title: Splunk Boss of the SOC (BOTS) Practice

tree.name: Alert Triage & Incident Investigation
tree.description: Learn the structured process of validating, enriching, prioritizing, and responding to security alerts. Master incident documentation, timeline creation, and effective communication during an incident using established frameworks.

resources.title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2 - Computer Security Incident Handling Guide

children.name: SOC Alert Triage Process
children.description: Understand the full lifecycle of an alert from generation to closure, including initial review, validation (true positive/false positive), severity classification, impact assessment, and initial containment steps. Learn to enrich alerts with threat intelligence and contextual data.

children.name: Incident Investigation & Playbooks
children.description: Investigate common incident scenarios like suspicious logins, malware infections, web attacks, and data exfiltration. Learn to follow and adapt structured incident response playbooks effectively, utilizing tools like EDR consoles, network sniffers, and sandboxes.

children.name: Network & Endpoint Investigation Techniques
children.description: Develop skills in investigating network traffic for suspicious patterns, analyzing endpoint logs and processes, and understanding how to leverage EDR/XDR solutions for deep dives into compromised systems. Focus on specific forensic artifacts from common operating systems.

resources.title: Analyzing Network Traffic for Malicious Activity

children.name: Basic Digital Forensics for Triage
children.description: Understand foundational concepts of digital forensics relevant to initial incident triage, including chain of custody, volatile data collection, basic disk image analysis, and memory forensics to preserve evidence for deeper analysis.

children.name: Incident Documentation & Reporting
children.description: Master the art of documenting evidence, creating clear timelines, assessing impact, classifying severity, and writing comprehensive case notes and post-incident reports. Understand escalation paths and effective communication with stakeholders.

tree.name: Advanced Threat Detection & Incident Response
tree.description: Transition from reacting to alerts to proactively engineering detections, hunting for threats, and leading full incident response efforts. This includes detection rule writing, tuning, advanced investigative techniques, and leveraging automation.

resources.title: Sigma Rules: Generic Signature Format for SIEM Systems
YARA: The Pattern Matching Swiss Knife for Malware Researchers
SANS FOR508: Advanced Incident Response, Threat Hunting, and Digital Forensics

children.name: Advanced Detection Engineering
children.description: Learn to design, implement, and fine-tune robust detection rules, distinguishing between signature, behavioral, and anomaly-based detections. Map detections to MITRE ATT&CK, perform threat modeling, and understand techniques like aggregation, baselining, and machine learning for enhanced detection.

children.name: Proactive Threat Hunting Methodologies
children.description: Develop proactive threat hunting skills using hypotheses, baselines, and advanced threat intelligence. Utilize various hunting frameworks (e.g., Hunt Chain), data sources, and analytical techniques to uncover hidden threats and unknown compromises within an environment.

children.name: Advanced Incident Response Management
children.description: Deep dive into the complete NIST incident response lifecycle: Preparation, Identification, Containment, Eradication, Recovery, and Post-Incident Activities (lessons learned, advanced forensic analysis, legal/compliance considerations, crisis communications).

resources.title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2 - Incident Response Lifecycle
SANS SEC504: Hacker Tools, Techniques, Exploits, and Incident Handling

children.name: Vulnerability & Threat Management
children.description: Understand the lifecycle of vulnerability management, including scanning, assessment, prioritization (e.g., CVSS, EPSS), remediation tracking, and patch management. Learn how vulnerability data feeds into threat detection and risk mitigation strategies for a SOC analyst.

children.name: Security Automation & Orchestration (SOAR)
children.description: Understand the concepts of Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR). Learn how SOAR platforms integrate with SIEM and other security tools to automate routine tasks, enrich alerts, streamline incident handling workflows, and create automated playbooks.

children.name: Cloud-Native Detection & Response
children.description: Focus on security operations within cloud environments. Understand cloud-native security services (e.g., AWS Security Hub, Azure Security Center, GCP Security Command Center), cloud log sources, serverless security, container security, and responding to incidents in a cloud-first infrastructure.

children.name: Introduction to Malware Reverse Engineering
children.description: Gain a basic understanding of reverse engineering concepts and tools (e.g., Ghidra, IDA Free, x64dbg) to perform deeper analysis of suspicious binaries, extract IOCs, and understand malware functionality beyond typical sandbox reports.

resources.title: Beginner's Guide to Reverse Engineering (Video Series)

tree.name: SOC Practical Skills & Career Readiness
tree.description: Apply learned concepts in practical lab environments, build a professional SOC portfolio, and prepare for interviews and certifications to launch and advance a successful career as a SOC Analyst.

children.name: Building a SOC Home Lab
children.description: Set up a virtualized home lab environment using tools like Security Onion, Splunk Free, Elastic Stack, or Wazuh. Practice data ingestion, alert generation, and incident investigation with simulated attacks (e.g., Atomic Red Team, Caldera).

resources.title: Configure a Splunk Home Lab for Blue Team
Setting up a Home SIEM (Elastic Stack)

children.name: SOC Portfolio Projects
children.description: Develop a strong professional portfolio by completing practical projects such as detailed alert triage write-ups, custom detection rule development, incident response playbooks, threat hunting reports, and post-incident analysis summaries. Showcase your work on platforms like GitHub.

children.name: Soft Skills & Professional Communication
children.description: Develop essential soft skills for a SOC analyst role, including critical thinking, problem-solving, attention to detail, teamwork, and effective communication (written and verbal) for incident reporting, stakeholder updates, and collaboration with other teams.

children.name: Career & Certification Preparation
children.description: Prepare for job interviews with common technical questions, scenario-based challenges, and behavioral questions. Understand relevant industry certifications (e.g., CompTIA CySA+, Splunk certifications, Microsoft SC-200, SANS GCIH) and strategies for continuous learning and career growth.

resources.title: Microsoft SC-200: Microsoft Security Operations Analyst
SOC Analyst Interview Questions and Answers
